To know which verbs take ESSERE in the passato prossimo: movement, change, staying (andare, nascere, restare).
To make the participle agree with the subject: andato / andata / andati / andate.
To put reflexive verbs in the past: mi sono alzato, ci siamo divertiti.
To choose correctly between AVERE and ESSERE.
To tell what happened, step by step (prima, poi, alla fine).
To say where and when you were born.
Tuesday, ten o'clock. Giulia walks into the workshop soaking wet. Professor Bellini looks at the clock.
Miss Esposito, it's ten o'clock. What happened this time?
Professor, I'm so sorry! This morning my alarm didn't go off and I got up at half past eight.
I washed and got dressed in five minutes, skipped breakfast and rushed out.
I got to the stop, but the bus left right in front of me!
It never came: there's a strike today! So I walked, in the rain.
On the bridge I slipped and fell into a puddle. Look at my trousers!
Hmm. And why didn't you phone?
My phone fell into the puddle with me. It died, poor thing.
(sighs) All right. Dry yourself off and start working. Matei, give her a coffee.
(quietly) So you were late because of the strike, the rain and the bridge.
Exactly. For once it's not my fault!
Don't swallow the final vowels: SO-no an-DA-to, SYA-mo par-TEE-ti. Italian pronounces every vowel clearly.
Two double consonants: CC + e is read "t" + "ch", and SS is a long "s": sut-CHES-so.
GH + e / i = a hard "g", as in Romanian "ghe": poz-ZAN-ghe-ra. And ZZ = a long "ts".
Most verbs form the passato prossimo with AVERE. ESSERE is used with verbs that have no direct object and that mainly express:
Movement from one place to another
andare, venire, arrivare, partire, entrare, uscire, tornare, cadere
A trick: if you can ask "whom? / what?" after the verb, it's almost certainly AVERE. "Ho mangiato (what?) una pizza", but "Sono andato (what?)" — impossible.
Careful: camminare (to walk), viaggiare (to travel), passeggiare (to stroll) take AVERE: "Ho camminato tanto."
With ESSERE the participle agrees with the subject, like an adjective: -o, -a, -i, -e.
A mixed group (Matei and Giulia) uses the masculine: "Matei e Giulia sono andati a Siena". Women only: "Giulia e Graziella sono andate".
Sono stato a Roma. (I've been to Rome.)
"Sono stato" is the participle for both ESSERE and STARE: "Sono stato a Roma" = "I've been to Rome", "Sono stato male" = "I was ill".
All reflexive verbs form the passato prossimo with ESSERE. The reflexive pronoun goes first, and the participle agrees with the subject:
In Romanian we say "m-am trezit" (with "a avea"), but in Italian it's "mi SONO alzato". Not "mi ho alzato"!
Connectors to link actions in order:
First I got up, then I got dressed.
After that I left the house.
In the end I arrived at ten.
Other useful words: all'improvviso (suddenly), per fortuna (luckily), purtroppo (unfortunately), finalmente (at last).
We had a great time at the party.
"I ate" or "I left"? Choose correctly: "Ieri ___ una pizza e poi ___ al cinema."

In November Giulia invited Matei to Naples for the birthday of her grandmother Assunta, who turned ninety.
They left on Friday evening on the fast train and arrived at the central station three hours later. Giulia's brother, Gennaro, came to pick them up in a little red car.
The traffic in Naples! Matei clung to his seat for twenty minutes. Gennaro, on the other hand, drove with one hand and talked on the phone with the other.
On Saturday morning they got up early and went for a walk along the seafront. Vesuvius appeared behind the clouds, big and calm.
At lunchtime all the relatives arrived: uncles, aunts, cousins, neighbours. Matei counted thirty-two people in a three-room flat.
Grandma Assunta was born in 1934 in Sorrento. She became a seamstress at fifteen and got married at twenty. She looked Matei up and down and said: "He's thin. Let him eat!"
Matei ate four plates of pasta, the parmigiana, the fish and three slices of cake. In the end he sat on his chair without speaking for half an hour.
On Sunday evening they went back to Florence. On the train Giulia fell asleep on Matei's shoulder. He didn't move for three hours, even though his arm went completely numb.
Before getting off, Giulia opened her eyes and said: "You know, Grandma asked me when I'm bringing you back."
Quanti anni ha compiuto la nonna Assunta?
Chi è venuto a prenderli alla stazione?

He carved the David at twenty-six. Then he went to Rome and painted the Sistine Chapel.
